name: Bilineal Acute Leukemia
aliases: Mixed Phenotype Acute Leukemia with Bilineal Features

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016) for Mixed Phenotype Acute Leukemia

criteria.description: Presence of two distinct blast populations each expressing lineage-specific markers for myeloid and lymphoid lineages
Immunophenotypic evidence demonstrating bilineal expression of myeloid and lymphoid markers on separate blast populations
Bone marrow aspirate showing ≥20% blasts with bilineal characteristics
Cytogenetic or molecular abnormalities supporting diagnosis (e.g., complex karyotype, BCR-ABL1 fusion)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of two distinct blast populations each expressing lineage-specific markers for myeloid and lymphoid lineages with ≥20% blasts in bone marrow
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires comprehensive immunophenotyping and morphological evaluation to distinguish bilineal from biphenotypic acute leukemia.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilineal blast populations in bone marrow
pathognomonic.notes: Distinct myeloid and lymphoid blast populations identified by immunophenotyping
searchTerms: two types of immature blood cells
pale skin and tiredness from anemia
fatigue and pallor due to low red blood cells
recurrent infections due to immune weakness
infections caused by low white blood cells

common.symptomName: Easy bruising and petechiae from thrombocytopenia
searchTerms: easy bruising and small red spots
petechiae and bleeding from low platelets

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement (e.g., cranial nerve palsies)

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing circulating blasts of two distinct lineages
Bone marrow biopsy with ≥20% blasts exhibiting bilineal immunophenotype
imaging: CT or MRI may reveal lymphadenopathy or organomegaly
Imaging to assess extramedullary disease (e.g., chloromas)
genetic: Possible presence of BCR-ABL1 fusion gene or other translocations
Molecular studies to exclude other leukemia subtypes
other: Flow cytometry demonstrating two distinct blast populations with lineage-specific markers

distinguishingFeatures: Single blast population co-expressing myeloid and lymphoid markers
Immunophenotypic overlap rather than two distinct blast populations
No evidence of myeloid lineage involvement

redFlags: Presence of two distinct blast populations on immunophenotyping
Failure to respond to standard single-lineage leukemia therapy
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the WHO classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Inaba H, et al. Mixed phenotype acute leukemia: clinical and biological features. Blood. 2018.
